content.value_statement: Teams often ship inconsistent UI because tokens, components, and documentation grow apart. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for scalable design systems.
actual_capabilities: Defines W3C-style design token structures for color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadows.
Shows React and TypeScript patterns for buttons, forms, cards, modals, and navigation.
Explains WCAG 2.1 AA guidance for contrast, keyboard behavior, ARIA, and semantic HTML.
Provides reusable templates for design tokens and component implementation.
Includes an audit checklist for tokens, components, patterns, documentation, and maintenance.
limitations: Does not execute commands or generate a complete package by itself.
Examples are generic and need adaptation to your stack, brand, and product rules.
Does not replace product research, visual design review, or usability testing.
Accessibility guidance still requires automated and manual validation in the target app.

use_cases.title: Start a New UI Kit
use_cases.description: Create token categories, base components, and documentation standards before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize Product Interfaces
use_cases.description: Align designers and engineers around shared tokens, component APIs, and accessibility requirements.

use_cases.title: Audit Component Quality
use_cases.description: Review an existing library for token coverage, component consistency, documentation, and WCAG gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Token Foundations
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new product interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-system-starter to propose color, typography, spacing, radius, and shadow tokens for a new web app.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Component APIs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate planning for a React component library.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-system-starter to define Button, Input, Card, Modal, and Navigation APIs with variants and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit of a current design system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-system-starter to audit my component library for token use, naming consistency, keyboard behavior, and documentation gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Adoption Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced rollout planning across multiple teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-system-starter to create a migration plan, governance rules, and documentation checklist for adopting our design system.

output_examples.input: Create foundations for a SaaS dashboard design system.
output_examples.output: A token plan covering semantic colors, type scale, spacing scale, radii, shadows, and contrast requirements.

output_examples.input: Define components for a shared React library.
output_examples.output: A component roadmap with Button, Input, FormField, Card, Modal, and Navigation patterns plus accessibility expectations.

output_examples.input: Audit our current UI kit before a redesign.
output_examples.output: A checklist-based review of token coverage, component consistency, documentation quality, theming, and WCAG compliance gaps.

best_practices: Start with tokens and naming rules before adding component variants.
Validate contrast, keyboard behavior, and labels for every interactive component.
Document component purpose, props, variants, accessibility, and examples together.
anti_patterns: Creating one-off component styles that bypass shared tokens.
Treating dark mode as a separate theme without shared semantic tokens.
Shipping components without usage guidance, deprecation rules, or accessibility notes.

faq.question: Does this skill create production code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates, examples, and guidance that you adapt to your project.

faq.question: Which frontend stack does it target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on React and TypeScript, but the token and documentation guidance is portable.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WCAG 2.1 AA, contrast, keyboard navigation, ARIA, and semantic HTML.

faq.question: Can it help with dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains semantic tokens, CSS variables, Tailwind dark mode, and theme provider patterns.

faq.question: Is this useful for existing design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the checklist to audit tokens, components, patterns, documentation, and maintenance practices.

faq.question: Does it connect to external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and templates. Links are references, not network actions.
